title: What goes into our post-tour follow-up

content.job: Standalone list email. Tell the full exchange from more tours and unanswered follow-up to the client's within-a-week practice and prospective texts. Connect the point to the complete LeadLock system with one reply invitation.
content.body:
She told me she pays attention to whether her venue is the first stop on a couple's tour list or the last one.

When she knows it's the last, she reaches out within a week. She asks, directly and politely, whether they've picked their venue or haven't decided yet. It's a question that fits a couple who has finished looking.

A couple fresh off their first tour is in a different place. They're still comparing, and they may not be ready to answer that.

**Knowing a couple toured your venue isn't the same as knowing they're ready to decide.**

She already had automated follow-up emails in place, and she was reaching out personally on top of them. She raised the idea of adding texts after the tour, and I agreed we could incorporate them.

That conversation is a good picture of how we think about follow-up. You're already generating inquiries, hosting tours and talking with couples yourself. The support around that work should build on what you learn during the visit, so a couple who's still comparing and a couple who's ready to decide each hear something that fits where they are.

LeadLock is the platform where we build your email and text follow-up. Inside it, we set up The Foolproof Follow-Up Advantage, our email-and-text follow-up system, around your own conversations. You run the platform, and the personal contact couples get from you stays yours.
content.ending:
If you'd like follow-up support shaped around what you learn on your tours, simply reply to this email and let's talk about your business.

Talk soon,
Whitney

That's the thinking behind our follow-up support. content.title: First tour or last tour
content.script:
I had a call with one of our venue clients recently, and she was booking more tours, but more of those couples were going quiet afterwards.

So I asked her a question. When couples leave a tour, do they still have other venues to see, or are they ready to move forward?

And she explained that she gauges one thing: is her venue their first tour, or their last?

When she knows it's their last, she reaches out within a week and asks, really politely, if they've made their choice or they're still undecided.

I thought that was such a smart distinction.

Because a couple who's just started touring is still comparing, right? They're not necessarily ready for that question yet.

Now, she already had automated emails going out, and she was following up personally on top of that. She'd been thinking about texting couples after the tour, too, and I told her we could add that.

So when we shape follow-up after a tour, the fact that a couple visited is only part of the picture. We want to know what they're ready to do next, so every email and text supports the conversation you're already having with them.

caption.body:
Couples found you, inquired and came out to see the venue in person. You walked them through it and helped them picture the day. Then some of them stop answering, and you're left guessing whether they're still deciding or have moved on.

I talked about this with one of our venue clients recently. Her tours were up, and so was the number of couples going quiet. I asked whether those couples left with other venues still to visit or ready to move forward.

She explained that she gauges where her venue falls in a couple's search. If it's their final visit, she follows up within a week and asks, kindly and plainly, whether they've made a decision or are still undecided. Someone at the start of their search isn't necessarily ready for that.

She already had automated emails working next to her own personal outreach, and when she raised adding post-tour texts, I agreed we could incorporate them.

What you learn on a tour tells us what the next message should make room for. The emails and texts support the contact you're already having with couples, at the point in the search they've actually reached.
caption.hook: When more couples tour your venue and more of them go quiet, it's worth asking where they were in their search.

When we're thinking about the follow-up, we need more than the fact that a couple visited. We want to know what they're ready to do, so the messages can support the conversation you're having with them.

content.title: A finished tour isn't a decision
content.script:
I don't think a completed venue tour tells you whether a couple is ready to book.

You can give two couples the same thoughtful tour, and they can leave in very different places. One still has other venues on the list. The other has seen everything and is close to choosing.

So before we shape follow-up for a venue, we want to know which couple we're talking to.

One of our venue clients does this really well. She had more tours and more couples going quiet, and when I asked her about it, she told me she reads whether her venue is early in a couple's search or the last stop. When it's the last stop, she checks in within a week and asks, nicely and directly, if they've picked a venue or are still deciding.

That question fits the end of a search. A couple who's still comparing isn't necessarily ready for it.

She was already pairing automated emails with her own personal follow-up, and when she brought up adding texts after the tour, I agreed we could fold those in.

That's how I think about follow-up. The emails and texts should carry what you learned on the tour, and you keep the conversation going with the couple.

caption.body:
You give every couple a thoughtful tour. Some leave with more venues on their list. Some have already seen everything and are close to choosing. From the outside, the quiet afterwards can look exactly the same.

That's why I want to know what a couple was ready to do before we shape any follow-up.

One of our venue clients had more tours and more unanswered messages, so I asked her about it. She distinguishes the start of a couple's tour list from the end. When she knows she was the final stop, she checks in politely within a week to ask if they've picked a venue or are still deciding. That direct question fits because they've finished visiting.

She also raised adding texts after the tour to the automated emails and personal follow-up she already had, and I agreed those could be included.

For us, the starting point is what the venue already knows about the couple. When follow-up matches how far along they are, it leaves room for the conversations you still want to have with them.
caption.hook: A couple can love your venue tour and still have other venues to see.

brief_copy.script:
When more venue tours come with more couples going quiet, I want to know what those couples were ready to do when they left.

Because you can give two couples a really thoughtful tour, and they can leave with very different things still ahead of them.

One has other venues to see. The other has finished touring and is closer to choosing.

I asked a venue client about that. She explained that she gauges whether her venue is their first tour or their last. After a last tour, she politely asks within a week whether they've picked a venue or are still deciding.

Someone who's still comparing venues may not be ready for the same conversation as someone who's seen every venue on their list.

caption.body:
When you're hosting more tours, you want the follow-up to carry forward the care you put into each visit. That includes leaving room for couples who are still comparing venues.

A venue client was seeing more tours and more unanswered messages. I asked what couples were ready to do afterwards, rather than assume the visit meant they were ready to book.

She explained that she distinguishes the start of their tour list from the end. After their final tour, she asks directly and politely, within a week, whether they've chosen or remain undecided. That question makes sense because she knows they've finished visiting venues.

She also raised adding post-tour texts to the automated emails and personal follow-up already in place. I agreed that those could be incorporated.

For us, the starting point is what the venue has learned from the couple. We want the messages supporting your follow-up to reflect where they are in their search, with room for the conversations you still need to have.

caption.body:
More tours are a good sign. But a tour on your calendar doesn't tell you whether the couple is on their first visit or their last, and unanswered follow-up looks the same either way.

This came up with one of our venue clients. I asked whether couples left planning other visits or ready to move forward. Her answer was that she watches whether her venue opened their search or closed it.

When she knows they've finished touring, she reaches out within a week and politely asks if they've landed on a venue or are still undecided. A couple who has only begun visiting is still comparing what they've seen.

She already paired automated emails with her personal contact, and she asked about texting couples after the tour as well. I said we could add that.

That's the kind of detail we want shaping the emails and texts around your conversations, so each couple hears from you in a way that suits how far their search has come.
